items.title: Magnarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: And what he did do was he turned me on to the right records. And that was the greatest lesson really I ever had, the first four or five times I went to his house. He did write some things out for me to practice.

ctx.x: Right. So if you asked Sal Amico about that, what did he tell you?

Well it’s funny I did sound him out about that. I did ask him. He never really told me. What he did was he accepted me for who I was, he didn’t [inaudible] me the situation. He understood my hunger for the music. And what he did do was he turned me on to the right records. And that was the greatest lesson really I ever had, the first four or five times I went to his house. He did write some things out for me to practice. He heard me play, you know I sat in in the club. So he knew where I was at. He gave me some…
Isn’t there something to be said though for getting that inspiration and then finding out on your own?
